findings.title: Accidental gitlink/submodule added to repository root
findings.body: This adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing only `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`, i.e. an accidental nested-repository gitlink unrelated to error upsampling. Merging it creates a bogus submodule entry at the repo root that can break checkouts/tooling expecting it to be a normal path and pollutes the tree; it should be removed from the PR.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses closure `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset` actually queried
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` (which `get_event_stats_factory` changes for dashboard discover-split widgets, e.g. passing `discover` or the original scoped dataset), but the eligibility check passes the outer closure variable `dataset`. When the two differ, counts are transformed for a dataset that is not being queried (e.g. upsampling a transactions/discover query, where `sample_weight` is invalid/zero) or not transformed for the errors query that is actually run, producing wrong counts or Snuba errors for split dashboard widgets.

findings.title: Error-focus check reads request.GET instead of the query actually being executed
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` only inspects `request.GET['query']`, ignoring the `query` argument passed to `_get_event_stats`. That argument is rewritten by callers (dashboard split builds `({query}) AND !event.type:transaction` and `({query}) AND event.type:transaction`, and event-stats can execute multiple/derived queries). Consequently a transaction-only subquery can be upsampled because the original request mentioned errors, while an error-only subquery whose request parameter is empty or formatted differently is not upsampled, yielding incorrect `sum(sample_weight)` counts for transactions or missed upsampling for errors.

findings.title: Allowlist eligibility is cached for 60s with a dead invalidation function and a hash()-based key
findings.body: Eligibility is stored under `error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}` for 60 seconds, but `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 67) is never called anywhere and no option-change hook invokes it, so removing a project from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` keeps inflating its counts (and adding one delays correct counts) until expiry. The key also relies on Python's built-in `hash()` of the project tuple rather than a stable, collision-resistant encoding of the project IDs (e.g. joining the sorted IDs), so distinct project sets can collide/share an eligibility decision within a process.

findings.title: upsampled_count sums sample_weight without coalescing missing weights to 1
findings.body: The new aggregate is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no `coalesce(sample_weight, 1)`/`ifNull` handling. The transform in error_upsampling.py applies it to every `count()` for an allowlisted project, including events ingested before client error sampling existed or sent by SDKs that did not set a client sample rate, whose `sample_weight` can be NULL. In ClickHouse `sum` over NULLs yields NULL/0 rather than counting those events as weight 1, so historical/unsampled errors silently disappear from upsampled timeseries instead of being counted once.

findings.title: Internal upsampled_count function is exposed as a public query function
findings.body: Unlike the neighbouring private internal function (which sets `private=True`), `upsampled_count` is registered without `private=True`, so any API user can send `upsampled_count()` directly as a y-axis/field on discover queries for arbitrary, non-allowlisted projects. That bypasses the all-projects-allowlisted and errors-only gating in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and returns misleading weighted counts (or errors on datasets without `sample_weight`); it should be marked private so only the server-side column transformation can invoke it.
